tagline: An AI money agent for college students that tells you how long your money lasts, and explains why, with proof.
track: The Agent That Can Explain Why

team.name: Evan Arghirescu
team.role: Product, agent orchestration, Zetaris and Meterless integration, UI

ai_provider.contract: Authorization: Bearer <runtime token>; meterless-app: runway on every request; meterless-scope: user on chat; GET /v1/models decides online / unauthorized / offline; 180 s timeout
where: meterless.py (connection, authorization, discovery, text-request checks, Auto Detect)
ui/provider.py (checks shown in Behind the scenes)
ai_provider.routed_model_shown: From meterless.compute_receipt.v1 (routed_model, receipt_id) on every answer: 'How Runway thought about this', Behind the scenes and logs/traces.jsonl
ai_provider.fallback: NVIDIA API directly, only when the Meterless Runtime is unreachable or refuses the token, labelled 'fallback' on the answer

nvidia_models.used_for: PLAN (picks 1-3 tools and their arguments as JSON, thinking off) and fast answers by default (EXPLAIN, thinking off)
nvidia_models.where: agent.py run(): PLAN call and explain_chain(think=False)

nvidia_models.used_for: Think harder answers (EXPLAIN, thinking on; its reasoning trace is shown in the app); also the fast-answer model in the live demo (FAST_EXPLAIN_MODEL, thinking off), because it ignores Nightshift's injected memories better (5/5 vs 2/5)

meterless_engines.implementation: hmem.py: a Python port of the reference in engines/hmem of github.com/Meterless/Meterless (Apache-2.0)
meterless_engines.feature: What Runway remembers: what the student marked done, what she opened (email draft, reminder, cancel page), her budget, planned shifts, preferences and short chat summaries, each with provenance and an append-only trust ledger; recalled into PLAN across sessions; the check-in asks 'Last time you clicked Form sent. Still true?'; Forget / This isn't right / Forget everything
meterless_engines.test: tests/test_hmem_conformance.py runs the official conformance vectors (engines/hmem/conformance/vectors/vectors.json, unchanged) with a Python port of runner.ts: 13/13 pass. tests/test_runway_memory.py: 8 tests for the product feature.

zetaris.role: The data layer: federated access over JDBC (Lightning SQL), one Lightning database per source
zetaris.federated_query: federated_recurring_charges: one statement across RUNWAY_CHECKING and RUNWAY_CARD (JOIN + UNION ALL + GROUP BY ... HAVING) to find charges that repeat every month
where: data_access.py (the 21 named queries; the app never runs ad-hoc SQL)
ui/live_zetaris.py ('Run live on Zetaris' button, uncached, with a timer)
zetaris.parity_test: tests/test_data_access.py::test_zetaris_parity: every named query returns the same rows on Zetaris and on the local files

cursor: Cursor was the development environment for the whole build. Runway's code was written by Claude Code running in Cursor's integrated PowerShell terminal; Cursor was used to open and run the project, watch Claude Code's changes and progress live, read and review the generated files, and run the app and tests. Cursor's own AI features (Composer, Grok) were not used for code generation.
sample_mode: SAMPLE_MODE=true (the default in .env.example, and when there is no .env): Maya's local files and recorded answers; no Zetaris, Nightshift or keys needed
traces: logs/traces.jsonl (one JSON line per live question: plan, tools, queries, model calls with routed model and receipt, timings, checks); example: docs/example_trace.json
data: Synthetic demo student (Maya). No real accounts connected.
